channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Huawei Found Guilty of US Charges in Landmark Case
item.description: Huawei Technologies Co. was found guilty of multiple US criminal charges, including money laundering, a conspiracy to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks about its business in Iran and North Korea. Bloomberg's Jill Disis has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Criticizes Australia Social Media Law as Harming Free Speech
item.description: The US ambassador to Australia said the country’s proposed legislation governing major technology firms will limit free speech and unfairly burden US companies, laying the groundwork for a dispute over the measure.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger and Angus Whitley

item.title: AI Chip Boom to See Won Build on Best Year in Almost a Decade
item.description: South Korea’s AI chip windfall is unleashing a wave of year-end currency flows, potentially pushing the won into its next phase of gains.
item.dc:creator: Hooyeon Kim

item.title: Alibaba in Talks for Potential Yuan, Dollar Bond Sale Next Year
item.description: Chinese e-commerce and cloud services giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. has been in discussions in recent weeks with banks about potentially raising money in the offshore bond markets next year, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang and Dong Cao

item.title: Japan Stocks’ Rebound Threatened as Retail Margin Losses Balloon
item.description: Japanese stocks may struggle to extend their rebound as ballooning unrealized losses among leveraged retail investors threaten to unleash further selling pressure.
item.dc:creator: Momoka Yokoyama and Kentaro Tsutsumi

item.title: Dell in Strong Position With No Signs of a Slowdown, CFO Says
item.description: Dell Technologies CFO David Kennedy says the company is in a strong position going into the fourth quarter. Dell boosted its fiscal year revenue sales outlook for the third time due to surging server sales fueled by the build-out of AI data centers. He speaks on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kinship Ventures Co-Founders Gwyneth Paltrow & Moj Mahdara on Partnership & Portfolio Strategy
item.description: Gwyneth Paltrow, Co-Founder & General Partner of Kinship Ventures and CEO and Founder of Goop Inc, and Moj Mahdara, Co-Founder & Managing Partner of Kinship Ventures, joined Bloomberg’s Romaine Bostick to discuss the venture capital firm’s approach to early and late stage investing, the names in their portfolio, the future of wellness and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bernstein’s Rasgon on What Jensen Huang’s Return Means for NVDA
item.description: Stacy Rasgon, a Senior Analyst covering Semiconductors at Bernstein, discusses whether recent events involving Nvidia and Jensen Huang have exposed weaknesses in the semiconductor trade. He discusses what the hyperscaler buildout will look at in 2028 and beyond. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Foxconn Faces India Insolvency Lawsuit Over Unpaid Vendor Dues
item.description: About half a dozen vendors in India are experiencing payment delays by Foxconn Technology Group’s local unit, said people familiar with the matter, with one even filing an insolvency lawsuit to recover $15 million in unpaid dues.
item.dc:creator: Alisha Sachdev

item.title: AI Stocks Retreat as Markets Rotate Beyond Tech
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Manulife John Hancock Investments Co-Chief Investment Strategist Emily Roland, JPMorgan Head of US High-Grade Credit Strategy Nathaniel Rosenbaum, The Conference Board Chief Economist, Leader of Economy, Strategy & Finance Center Dana Peterson, CUNY Graduate Center Research Professor, Economics Paul Krugman, Schwab Center for Financial Research Head of Macro Research & Strategy Kevin Gordon, Bernstein Research Senior Analyst Stacy Rasgon, Bank of America Business Banking President Sharon Miller, Kinship Ventures Co-Founder & General Partner Gwyneth Paltrow & Co-Founder & Managing Partner Moj Mahdara, & Butterball CEO Jay Jandrain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: J.P. Morgan Asset Mgmt’s Rosenbaum on 2027 AI Spend
item.description: Nathaniel Rosenbaum, JPMorgan’s Head of U.S. High-Grade Credit Strategy, expects another busy year of AI-related borrowing but says issuance growth could crest during 2027. High-grade supply surged nearly three and a half times this year, he said; next year, it could reach a record $2.1 trillion without repeating that jump. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Pullback Raises the Cost of Data Center Financing
item.description: The recent pullback in AI stocks is spilling into credit markets, making some data center financing more expensive even as demand for computing power remains strong. MUFG Americas CFO Mark Thumser says lenders are becoming more selective and investors are demanding wider spreads and better terms. He also argues the massive AI infrastructure buildout remains a long-term, transformational trend. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss financing demand following Anthropic’s IPO, the outlook for global credit markets, and growing public resistance to data center development. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Defensive Assets Are Springing to Life: Emily Roland
item.description: Emily Roland, Co-Chief Investment Strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments, argues that the Federal Reserve is central to the outlook for equities as momentum in the AI trade slows and markets need a stronger macro cycle to advance. She says investors need a Fed “put,” not only support from Trump-related policy, and describes the Fed as a key market problem. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hackers Breach CIA System to Access Unclassified Information
item.description: An unclassified Central Intelligence Agency computer system was breached by hackers, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Jake Bleiberg

item.title: Crypto Winter Persists, 24/7 Trading Arrives, Kalshi Under Pressure
item.description: "Bloomberg Crypto" covers the people, transactions, and technology shaping the world of decentralized finance. Today's guests: Bullish President Stacey Cunningham, OKXice Co-Chair Andrew Cuomo, Bain Capital ventures Partner Matt Harris, NYU Faculty & Monarq Asset Management Chief Operating Officer Professor Ayesha Kiani, and Vanderbilt Law School Associate Dean & Professor of Law Yesha Yadav. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: HP Gives Profit Forecast Aiming Tighter Grip on Memory Costs
item.description: HP Inc. gave a profit forecast for the current year that will likely exceed analysts’ estimates, signaling the computer and printer maker is improving its ability to manage rising costs associated with memory chips.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Dell Raises Annual Sales Forecast Again on AI Server Demand
item.description: Dell Technologies Inc. boosted its fiscal year revenue sales outlook for the third time as the rapid build-out of AI data centers fuels surging server sales.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Ex-OpenAI Staffer Charged With Planting Bug Is Granted Bail
item.description: The former OpenAI staffer charged with bugging a company conference room was ordered to be released on a $1 million bond after a judge said he hasn’t seen enough evidence of wrongdoing to justify keeping the Saudi Arabian national locked up before trial.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg and Peter Blumberg

item.title: Nvidia Is a ‘Good Corporate Citizen,’ Attorney General Says
item.description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Nvidia Corp. is “a good corporate citizen,” while declining to directly answer questions about whether the Justice Department is scrutinizing the circumstances that led to the temporary exit of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Georgia Fearn and Chris Strohm

item.title: Xiaomi Shares Surge Due to Better-Than-Expected Phone Sales
item.description: Xiaomi Corp.’s shares surged in Hong Kong after the company reported a smaller-than-expected sales decline in the third quarter, a sign its effort to mitigate the impact from a global memory shortage paid off.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
